MSM8996 vendor PCIe API with native CCF/QMP resources
==================================================

compatible: "qcom,msm8996-pci-msm"

This is an extension of qcom,pci-msm for the actual MSM8996 Gen2 controller,
not a generic alias for newer SDM/QCS controllers. It retains the vendor
msm_pcie_* client, configuration recovery and link notification APIs used
by Sony BCMDHD, while obtaining PHY and power through real 4.19 providers.

Required native resources:
- phys = <&pciephy_0>; phy-names = "pciephy": the existing
  qcom,msm8996-qmp-pcie-phy lane, initialized and powered via the PHY API.
- power-domains = <&gcc PCIE0_GDSC>: real GCC genpd, acquired through
  runtime PM; do not describe the GDSC as an invented regulator supply.
- Vendor host clocks named pcie_0_aux_clk, pcie_0_cfg_ahb_clk,
  pcie_0_mstr_axi_clk, pcie_0_slv_axi_clk, pcie_0_ldo and pcie_0_pipe_clk.
  The generic QMP PHY owns its PIPE-clock enable/reset lifecycle.
- vreg-1p8/vreg-0p9 supplies and exact board voltage constraints.
- Legacy INTx mapping and optional int_pls_link_down dedicated interrupt.

The resource windows, IRQ numbers and regulator/GPIO wiring in the Tone
supplement come from Sony 4.4.302 commit
0c295b15b6d0fb59a64e13b9e0ef2070818ef2a1, principally
arch/arm/boot/dts/qcom/msm8996.dtsi and msm8996-tone-common.dtsi.
Its drivers/pci/host/pci-msm.c selects PARF DBI/slave-window offsets
0x168/0x16c for MSM8996, unlike the newer vendor defaults 0x350/0x358.
The old interrupt-map entry10 (int_pls_link_down) selects GIC SPI254;
SPI250 is int_pme_legacy and must not be used for link-down.
The old root-port PCI device ID is 17cb:0104. Gen3 preset programming and
the newer PARF device-type register are not applied to this Gen2 path.

The supplement removes the alternative fixed WLAN regulator owning GPIO84
before adding the real android,bcmdhd_wlan platform node. The retained Sony
controlfnc implementation is the sole GPIO84 owner and invokes the vendor
host enumerate/PM APIs. GPIO79 is the real WLAN host-wake line.

No PHY-ready, regulator or link-success result is synthesized. Provider
errors propagate. PCIe link training, actual DMA, wakeup, suspend/resume and
linkdown recovery still require testing on the physical Sony board.
